results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Optional (if object fields/relationships are uncertain)] [Prerequisite]: Inspect available fields using SALESFORCE_GET_ALL_FIELDS_FOR_OBJECT (avoid invalid field selections later).
[Required] [Step]: Search for the target account using SALESFORCE_SEARCH_ACCOUNTS (use lightweight identifiers and request only minimal fields needed to confirm the match).
[Required] [Next Step]: Search for the target deal using SALESFORCE_SEARCH_OPPORTUNITIES (scope by the confirmed account when possible; keep the fields list minimal for faster disambiguation).
[Required] [Next Step]: Retrieve the full account record by ID using SALESFORCE_GET_ACCOUNT (after confirming the correct account_id).
[Required] [Next Step]: Retrieve the full deal record by ID using SALESFORCE_GET_OPPORTUNITY (after confirming the correct opportunity_id).

[Optional (if you also need associated contacts/roles)] [Next Step]: Pull contact-role rows tied to the deal(s) using SALESFORCE_RUN_SOQL_QUERY (optionally selecting relationship fields), or use SALESFORCE_GET_RELATED_LIST_RECORDS_CONTACTS when the requirement is framed as related-list retrieval with pagination.
[Optional (if you have many record IDs to hydrate)] [Next Step]: Bulk-fetch records by ID using SALESFORCE_GET_COMPOSITE_SOBJECTS (reduce per-record GET calls).

[Required] [Fallback]: If search results are ambiguous or require more precise filtering/joins, use SALESFORCE_RUN_SOQL_QUERY (or SALESFORCE_LIST_OPPORTUNITIES for paging through deal candidates) to identify the correct IDs before fetching full records.
[Required] [Step]: Retrieve parties using CAPSULE_CRM_LIST_PARTIES (page through results as needed, then keep only records whose party type is an organisation).

[Optional (if you need server-side filtering such as by tag or complex criteria)] [Fallback]: Query matching parties using CAPSULE_CRM_RUN_FILTER_QUERY (paginate with page/perPage, then still confirm the returned party type is an organisation).
[Optional (if validating relationships for a chosen organisation)] [Next Step]: List linked people using CAPSULE_CRM_LIST_ORG_EMPLOYEES (useful to confirm members/employees before further actions).
[Optional (if enriching or correcting organisation details)] [Next Step]: Update the organisation using CAPSULE_CRM_UPDATE_PARTY (confirm field changes before writing).
known_pitfalls: [SALESFORCE_GET_ACCOUNT] Full-record responses can be extremely wide; downstream processing may be heavy if you don’t constrain fields earlier during SALESFORCE_SEARCH_ACCOUNTS.
[SALESFORCE_RUN_SOQL_QUERY] Relationship field selections can return nested objects and null subfields; consumers should handle missing keys and nested dictionaries safely.
[SALESFORCE_GET_RELATED_LIST_RECORDS_CONTACTS] Related-list retrieval may require pagination to return all rows; ensure callers are prepared to iterate until completion.
[CAPSULE_CRM_LIST_PARTIES] Returns mixed party types; you must filter by the party type field to output organisations only.
[CAPSULE_CRM_RUN_FILTER_QUERY] Can fail with HTTP 500 in some sessions; keep CAPSULE_CRM_LIST_PARTIES as the reliable default path.
[CAPSULE_CRM_RUN_FILTER_QUERY] Results may appear under a nested raw payload (e.g., response.data.raw.parties) rather than a simpler parties field.
[CAPSULE_CRM_LIST_ORG_EMPLOYEES] Only meaningful for organisation parties; using a non-organisation selection can return empty or irrelevant data.

SALESFORCE_SEARCH_ACCOUNTS.description: Search for Salesforce accounts using criteria like name, industry, type, location, or contact information. Always provide at least one filter parameter; omitting all filters returns a broad, slow listing. Owner/territory filtering is unsupported — use SALESFORCE_RUN_SOQL_QUERY for ownership-based filters. Use SALESFORCE_GET_ACCOUNT to fetch complete field data for a specific record. Unsupported filter fields may be silently ignored — verify results reflect intended criteria.

name.description: Search by account name. Supports partial matches.

type.description: Search by account type. Note: The Type field may not exist in all Salesforce orgs. If the query fails with 'No such column Type', either omit this parameter or use a custom Type__c field if available in your org.

limit.description: Maximum number of accounts to return. Results are hard-capped at approximately 2000 rows; use more selective filters if the full dataset exceeds this.

phone.description: Search by phone number. Supports partial matches. Requires field-level security access to the Phone field.

fields.description: Comma-separated list of valid Salesforce Account field API names to retrieve. Only use actual field names like Id, Name, Industry, etc. Do not include type annotations or placeholders like <string> or <DATE_TIME>. If any field in this list is restricted by field-level security, the entire request will fail — use a minimal set of standard fields (e.g., Id,Name,Website) when access is uncertain.

website.description: Search by website. Supports partial matches.

billing_city.description: Search by billing city. Supports partial matches.

billing_state.description: Search by billing state/province. Supports partial matches.

billing_country.description: Search by billing country. Supports partial matches.

SALESFORCE_SEARCH_OPPORTUNITIES.description: Search for Salesforce opportunities using multiple criteria like name, account, stage, amount, close date, or status. Apply at least one filter to avoid broad result sets. Partial-match searches may return multiple similar records; verify the correct record by Id before downstream use.

name.description: Search by opportunity name. Supports partial matches.

limit.description: Maximum number of opportunities to return. Maximum value is 2000. When totalSize in the response exceeds limit, use nextRecordsUrl to paginate through the full dataset.

fields.description: Comma-separated list of Opportunity fields to retrieve. Supports direct Opportunity fields (e.g., Id, Name, Amount) and parent relationship fields (e.g., Account.Name, Owner.Name). Note: Contact.* fields (Contact.Name, Contact.Email, etc.) are NOT valid because Opportunity does not have a direct parent relationship to Contact; use OpportunityContactRole queries to get contact information. Parent relationship fields like Account.Name may be null on returned records; guard against missing nested values when post-processing.

is_won.description: Filter by won status. True for won opportunities, False for lost (only applies to closed opportunities).

is_closed.description: Filter by closed status. True for closed opportunities, False for open.

account_name.description: Search by associated account name. Supports partial matches.

close_date_to.description: Search opportunities with close date before this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

close_date_from.description: Search opportunities with close date from this date (YYYY-MM-DD). When computing relative ranges (e.g., 'this week'), derive dates using the user's local timezone to avoid off-by-one-day errors.

SALESFORCE_GET_ACCOUNT.description: Retrieves a specific account by ID from Salesforce, returning all available fields.

account_id.description: The Salesforce ID of the account to retrieve.

SALESFORCE_GET_OPPORTUNITY.description: Retrieves a specific opportunity by ID from Salesforce, returning all available fields.

fields.description: Comma-delimited string of Opportunity field API names to retrieve. If omitted, all fields are returned. Custom objects may use non-standard API names for common fields (e.g., primary contact); verify exact field API names and handle null values.

opportunity_id.description: The Salesforce ID of the opportunity to retrieve. Must be a valid 15 or 18 character alphanumeric Salesforce ID (e.g., '006Wd000005FG3CIAW'). When multiple similarly named opportunities exist in search results, confirm the correct record by `Id` or other key attributes before passing the ID here.

CAPSULE_CRM_LIST_PARTIES.description: Tool to list all parties (contacts) on the account. Use when you need to fetch contacts with optional filters or embed additional related data.

page.description: Page number of results to return (>=1). Default: 1.

embed.description: Comma-separated list of additional data to embed. Allowed values: 'tags', 'fields', 'organisation', 'missingImportantFields'.

since.description: Include only parties changed after this date (ISO8601 format).

perPage.description: Number of parties per page (1-100). Default: 50.

CAPSULE_CRM_RUN_FILTER_QUERY.description: Tool to run structured filter queries on parties, opportunities or kases. Use when you need to retrieve entities matching specific filter conditions.

page.description: Page of results to return. Default is 1.

embed.description: Additional data to include, comma-separated list. Supported values vary by entity.

entity.description: Entity type to filter: parties, opportunities, or kases (projects).

field.description: Field name to filter on (case-sensitive). Examples for parties: 'name', 'email', 'phone', 'city', 'state', 'country', 'zip', 'type', 'tag', 'owner', 'team', 'jobTitle', 'addedOn', 'updatedOn', 'lastContactedOn'. Boolean fields: 'hasEmailAddress', 'hasPhoneNumber', 'hasAddress', 'hasPeople', 'hasTags'. Organization fields use 'org.' prefix: 'org.name', 'org.tag'. Custom fields use 'custom:{fieldId}' or 'org.custom:{fieldId}' format. Note: Address fields like city, state, country, zip are top-level fields, NOT nested (use 'state' not 'address.state'). Country must be an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g., 'US', 'GB', 'CA').

value.description: Value to compare the field against. Type depends on the field and operator.

operator.description: Operator to use. All fields support: 'is', 'is not'. String fields also support: 'starts with', 'ends with', 'contains'. Number fields also support: 'is greater than', 'is less than'. Date fields also support: 'is after', 'is before', 'is older than', 'is within last', 'is within next'.

conditions.description: List of filter conditions combined with 'and'.

filter.description: Filter object containing conditions and optional sort order.

perPage.description: Number of entities per page (1-100). Default is 50.

SALESFORCE_RUN_SOQL_QUERY.description: Executes a SOQL query against Salesforce data. Returns records matching the query with pagination support.

examples: SELECT Id, Name, Email FROM Contact WHERE CreatedDate > 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z
SELECT Name, (SELECT LastName FROM Contacts) FROM Account
SELECT COUNT() FROM Lead WHERE Status = 'New'
SELECT COUNT(Id), StageName FROM Opportunity GROUP BY StageName
SELECT Id, Name FROM Opportunity ORDER BY Amount DESC LIMIT 10
SELECT Id, Name FROM Contact WHERE LastName = 'O\'Brien'
SELECT Id, Name, Description FROM Account LIMIT 10
query.description: SOQL query to execute. Must start with SELECT. Field names must match object schema exactly — use SALESFORCE_GET_ALL_FIELDS_FOR_OBJECT for unfamiliar objects. ALIASES: No 'AS' keyword (use 'SUM(Amount) TotalSales' NOT 'SUM(Amount) AS TotalSales'). AGGREGATES: Without GROUP BY, ORDER BY/LIMIT not allowed (single-row result). COUNT() SYNTAX: Bare COUNT() only valid alone. With GROUP BY or other fields, must specify field: COUNT(Id) or COUNT(fieldName). Example: 'SELECT COUNT(Id), Status FROM Lead GROUP BY Status' NOT 'SELECT COUNT(), Status FROM Lead GROUP BY Status'. NON-GROUPABLE: Long text, rich text, encrypted text, compound address/location fields. NON-FILTERABLE: Long text area, rich text, encrypted text, multi-select picklists, blob fields CANNOT be in WHERE. FIELDS(ALL)/FIELDS(CUSTOM) require LIMIT ≤200. ID values need single quotes. Apostrophes use backslash: 'O\'Brien'.
